newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour - UK competitiveness key to EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour - UK competitiveness key to EMU entry.

text.p: Labour's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said on Thursday that a Labour government would decide whether or not to join a single European currency on the basis of Britain's ability to compete in Europe.

"Labour's commitment to a single currency rests on the condition that we must first achieve convergence in the real economic world of industrial output, investment, skills, technology....and of course jobs," Cook told a meeting of the European movement, a group that argues the case for Britain's continued role in Europe.
Cook added that it was a decision which required "a timetable that allows those responsible to weigh it carefully, to debate it properly."

The Times newspaper reported on Thursday that the Labour leadership, including Cook, was edging towards a decision to stay out of a single currency when it first begins, probably in 1999, because it would be too controversial a decision to take so early in the new administration.
Senior Labour sources on Thursday dismissed the story as press speculation, saying no decision had been taken.

Cook said the decision was one which required careful consideration adding, "it is very important that it is not a decision that we are bounced into by the timescales of broadcasters and the deadlines of the media."
General elections are due by May 1997 with the Labour Party well ahead in opinion polls.

Labour's policy on a single currency is that it will keep its options open and any decision to enter will be taken with the country's approval, either through a referendum or through a manifesto commitment in a general election.
The Times said there was debate as to whether or not the manifesto for the coming general election should give an exclusive commitment on a single currency or not.
Cook merely repeated Labour's policy, saying "we will make sure we have the consent of the British people."
